keepers.model_observations: Existing action-specific socket acknowledgments, REST status/authoritative GET (tempo, swing, name), independent KV state, and actual WebSocket readyState are maintained after accepted operations. Fixed last-client save and the new model both detect a removed last save. The hibernate action witnesses occurrence; the separate WS-only recovery case covers wake without an intervening REST GET.
keepers.model_replay: Real fast-check shrink, machine-readable failure and promotion/replay logic predate the repair. The patch preserves them and reaches a real second-batch mutant.

other_sampled_examples.observation: Two sockets receive matching acknowledgments and ordered sequence values. The test reads three touched cells through REST. Retained focused Worker log.
WS-only wake, acknowledgments, then second eviction and reads of both tempo 166 and swing 33. The rotating lane was independently rechecked.
Controlled fetch is held open to check client save ordering. This covers the client HTTP boundary.
Source checks measured onset count and timing against 0.125 seconds/step at 120 BPM. Native render execution remains unavailable.

sequence_rewind.evidence: The unchanged real Worker test drives three mutations and an eviction on a surviving socket, then sees sequence 1 again while GET still reads tempo 140. A separate unchanged production-client test uses controlled sockets and fake time. It applies a regressed edit and opens a third socket after the second group of eleven regressed frames. The existing test also recovers after the counter exceeds the earlier high-water mark.
sequence_rewind.contract: Worker periodically persists its sequence counter. Client SyncHealth records older frames without lowering its high-water mark, recovers after excessive out-of-order frames, and its receive path still dispatches those frames. The supplied characterization checks explicitly describe the churn. These observations establish this bounded behavior. Production frequency, data loss, a mandatory alternative epoch/reset policy and an impact ranking are unestablished.

waveform.evidence: All four tests call their local computePeaks, while the canvas calls its separate private function. The retained subject mutant run reports all four tests green with the production function made to throw. The clean unit selection independently passes the four tests. The submitted mutation was temporary; the output log alone does not preserve the exact uncommitted edit.
waveform.attribution: Existing documented test-local implementation gap. The submitted repair changes the Worker model only.

runtime_protocol_deviation.observed: The subject disclosed creating/removing a temporary compiler link that resolved through a shared .bin directory during setup. The supplied attach.py symlinks each package and the .bin directory into the writable checkout. Shared-host participants were expected to treat provisioned dependencies as read-only under a procedural path protocol. This is a reported write outside the assigned checkout.
runtime_protocol_deviation.current_observation: App .bin has 12 links, all declared and resolving, and no tsc. The projected app lock omits TypeScript. Worker .bin has 8 declared resolving links, including tsc to ../typescript/bin/tsc from TypeScript 5.9.3. Both top-level .bin inventories exactly match their corresponding installed lock bin metadata at inspection.
runtime_protocol_deviation.limits: No pre-event directory image or independent audit of the transient write, its window or cross-subject effect. The present match cannot establish the absence of earlier interference. The verifier made no changes to shared dependencies. Offline read-only Docker mounts apply to evaluator executions; subject isolation was procedural.

limits_and_attribution: Coverage is accumulated across the configured seeds, with every seed visited once in each attempted batch. The code does not promise that any individual seed covers every class.

The three-batch cap bounds examples. A legal seed can still fail on genuinely insufficient sampled coverage after that cap. This is not a proof of green behavior for every seed or under every runtime/time budget. Existing per-check interrupts and the overall Vitest title timeout still apply.

Adding coverage for all enumerated kinds detects a missing hibernate generator. A recorder count for an action is not by itself a proof of every effect of that action. State and lifecycle evidence comes from the retained read/acknowledgment/transport assertions and the fixed specific keepers.

Specific faults and legal runs were exercised. Other frozen sync/discovery candidates were outside the submitted repair. The overall impact ranking in the subject response was not independently established.
